task: Refine the round-02 convergence figure using visual grouping and annotation methods observed in a supplied high-quality journal reference, while preserving the input data and scientific scope.
title: Objective trajectories and signed updates
data_source: examples/data/convergence_practice.csv, carried forward unchanged from round 02
objective: Show the displayed objective trajectories as the visual priority, while retaining only the independent signed-update evidence needed to interpret the one non-monotone step.
core_conclusion: Within the displayed illustrative trajectories, all three methods end below their displayed starting values; the Proposed trace ends at the lowest shown objective, and its only positive adjacent update is visible in the supporting panel without being promoted to a general performance claim.
claim: Within the displayed illustrative trajectories, all three methods end below their displayed starting values; the Proposed trace ends at the lowest shown objective, and its only positive adjacent update is visible in the supporting panel without being promoted to a general performance claim.
audience: Readers of a mathematical modelling or algorithm research paper

canvas.intended_placement: double-column figure; single-column preview is a stress test

layout.label: a
layout.content: Observed current objective across ten iterations, with concise panel title, direct terminal labels, and a quiet open marker for the single current-versus-running-best divergence.

layout.label: b
layout.content: Signed adjacent-step objective changes on the same iteration scale, with a zero reference and one restrained +0.02 annotation.

evidence_panels.question: What objective trajectories are actually observed over the displayed window?
Where do adjacent raw updates decrease or increase the minimized objective?

reference_image.description: Supplied Figure 3 from Deep active optimization for complex systems

encoding.algorithm: consistent restrained color plus marker shape across panels
encoding.historical_best: one small open marker at the single Proposed point where it differs from current; coincident values are not redundantly overplotted
encoding.delta_objective: signed y-position relative to a zero reference
encoding.direction: lower objective is better; negative delta is a decrease

uncertainty.reason: The input has one deterministic practice trajectory per algorithm and no replicate or error estimate.

design_decisions: Kept two panels because signed updates provide independent evidence about the one local positive step.
Removed the round-02 long figure-level statement and replaced it with concise panel titles inspired by the reference figure's text hierarchy.
Reduced the iteration-6 incumbent annotation to a quiet marker and left the signed +0.02 label in the supporting panel.
Borrowed grouping, direct labels, aligned axes, and restrained local callouts from the reference without copying its data, colors, panel count, or scientific claims.
limitations: This practice dataset cannot support general algorithm performance claims.
A single-column placement is a stress test; double-column width is the intended use for this information density.
The external reference provides visual methods only and is not a source of data for this figure.
review_risks: The label Proposed must not be interpreted as validated superiority.
The signed delta convention must remain explicit because the objective is minimized.
The quiet incumbent marker must not be mistaken for a new measured series.
The reference image must remain outside the output figure and no reference uncertainty must be copied.
scientific_unknowns: No repeated runs, seeds, benchmark context, or real-unit interpretation are provided.
No stopping criterion or target threshold is defined.
The table does not establish performance outside the displayed ten iterations.
user_reference_note: The supplied reference image was viewed and analyzed for visual methods only; it was not copied, embedded, or marked as a favorite.
